definitions.explanation: A punishment imposed by law for committing a crime, including fines, imprisonment, and other legal penalties.

examples.japanese: {厳|きび}しい{刑罰|けいばつ}が{科|か}される。
{刑罰|けいばつ}の{目的|もくてき}は{犯罪|はんざい}の{抑止|よくし}だ。
examples.english: The purpose of criminal punishment is the deterrence of crime.

examples.japanese: この{国|くに}では{薬物|やくぶつ}{犯罪|はんざい}に{対|たい}する{刑罰|けいばつ}が{非常|ひじょう}に{重|おも}い。
examples.english: In this country, criminal punishments for drug offenses are extremely heavy.

notes:
A formal legal term composed of {刑|けい} (punishment/penalty) and {罰|ばつ} (punishment). Used primarily in legal, political, and academic contexts when discussing the justice system.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {刑罰|けいばつ}を{科|か}す: to impose a punishment
- {刑罰|けいばつ}を{受|う}ける: to receive a punishment
- {刑罰|けいばつ}を{軽|かる}くする: to lighten a punishment
- {厳|きび}しい{刑罰|けいばつ}: severe punishment
- {刑罰|けいばつ}{制度|せいど}: penal system

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {罰|ばつ}: punishment — more general, used for any punishment including informal ones
- {刑|けい}: sentence, penalty — the specific court-imposed sentence (e.g., {懲役|ちょうえき}{刑|けい} "prison sentence")
- {処罰|しょばつ}: punishment, penalization — slightly broader, includes disciplinary actions
- {罰則|ばっそく}: penal provisions — the rules defining punishments in law
